answer: Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 255 answers need 255 separate inference runs with separate seeds. Because the island index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the mesa audit republishes the full set. Reusing one run across aliases collides on the dune identifier and voids the later submissions, as a result the operator burns for 255 runs and collects one. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
